paras: The posse shooting of Scott Lanier's assailant took place in July 1881 in the "tenth ward" of a Louisiana parish, when a constable and posse pursued and shot an unnamed Black man accused of shooting Scott Lanier. First reported as "fatally wounded," the man was described three weeks later as alive after the amputation of an arm, while Lanier had recovered.

According to an item credited to the Morehouse Clarion, "a colored man" shot and dangerously wounded "Mr. Scott Lanier" on a Tuesday in the tenth ward, a man with whom he had "previously had a difficulty." He was said to have fired four shots, twice with a shotgun and twice with a pistol, and eight bullets struck Lanier.

The man fled and was pursued by the Constable and a posse, who overtook him the same Tuesday night. In the report's words, "refusing to surrender," he "was fired upon and fatally wounded." Only this version, from the pursuers' side, appears in the coverage, which does not name him.

The Constable also arrested another Black man, charged with being accessory to the shooting of Lanier, and lodged him in jail. On August 20 a follow-up reported that the man "whom the constable's posse shot in capturing him" had his arm amputated, that gangrene had set in, and that physicians expected another amputation. Lanier, the item said, had recovered; no report of a death or a trial appears in the coverage.

The episode is known from two short items in the Donaldsonville Chief's columns of Louisiana state news. The July 30 item ran under a Morehouse Clarion heading beside a lightning strike and a marshal's appointment; the August 20 follow-up carried no credit. Neither item carried a headline or comment; both gave Lanier the courtesy title "Mr." while calling the other man "a colored man" and "the Negro," and the first accounted for the posse's firing by his refusal to surrender.
The first item called the man "fatally wounded"; the later report, describing him alive and under treatment weeks afterward, is the better evidence of his condition.

reader.title: Posse shooting of Scott Lanier's assailant
bases: A constable and posse pursued and shot a Black man accused of shooting Scott Lanier when he refused to surrender (A2); a later report says he survived with an amputated arm (A3), so the episode is a posse shooting rather than a killing.

The first report called the man 'fatally wounded' (A2), but three weeks later he was reported alive after an arm amputation (A3), and no death is reported. The shooting was by a constable and posse making an arrest of a fugitive, not a group acting outside the law (A2, A3).
Both reports are state-news gleanings in one paper, the Donaldsonville Chief, the first credited to the Morehouse Clarion (A2) and the follow-up uncredited (A3); no other paper's account was found.
